contributions.headingText: Intranodal palisaded myofibroblastoma is a benign, lymph node–based smooth muscle / myofibroblastic stromal neoplasm.
2E84.Y Benign fibrogenic or myofibrogenic tumour of other specified sites

Acceptable: intranodal/nodal myofibroblastoma; nodal myofibroblastoma; palisaded myofibroblastoma.

Not recommended: intranodal haemorrhagic spindle cell tumour with amianthoid fibres.

Inguinal lymph nodes are principally involved {2712187; 2712186; 8804479; 1594491; 25025452}, with rare examples described in axillary, neck, submandibular, para-oesophageal, retroperitoneal, and mediastinal nodes {23317593; 25025452; 2332214; 31400261; 21718465; 17284119}.
Patients present with a solitary, rarely multicentric mass, which is slow-growing, painless or (less often) tender, and mobile {17284119; 23714684; 25025452}.

The tumour occurs in patients aged 19–78 years {17284119; 23714684; 25025452}, with peak incidence in the fifth and sixth decades of life {17284119; 25025452}. The M:F ratio is 2:1 {17284119; 8804479; 1594491; 25025452}, and there is no racial predilection {17284119}.

The etiology is unknown. It has been suggested that trauma, drainage of mutagenic factors, and/or inflammation potentially induce CTNNB1 mutations in lymph node myoid stromal cells {2712186; 25025452}.
Gain-of-function CTNNB1 exon 3 missense mutations in codon 32, 33, 34, or 37 result in β-catenin–induced upregulation of cyclin D1 and cellular proliferation {12873184; 25025452}.

Lymph nodes usually measure 6–50 mm {2712187; 2712186; 1594491; 25025452}. The cut surface shows one or more tumour nodules separated from compressed lymphoid tissue by fibrous bands. Nodules are white-grey with dark-red haemorrhagic areas {17284119; 23714684}.

Tumour nodules are composed of moderately to highly cellular short fascicles, which are focally fibromatosis-like, and whorls of spindled cells. Variably shaped, dense collagenous bodies and vessels with hyalinized walls are present, on which the tumour cells may show vague nuclear palisading. The tumour cells have scant, lightly eosinophilic cytoplasm {2712187; 2712186; 1594491; 16821615; 8316966; 25025452}. Perinuclear vacuoles and rounded, salmon-coloured intracytoplasmic inclusions are common {2712187; 2712186; 25025452}. The elongated, focally wavy nuclei are cytologically bland, and mitotic activity ranges from 0 to 8 mitoses/5 mm2 {2712186; 25025452}. The stromal matrix is finely collagenous to myxocollagenous, with extravasated erythrocytes and/or haemosiderin commonly encountered. A major differential diagnosis is Kaposi sarcoma.

Immunohistochemically, the tumour cells diffusely express vimentin, SMA, and MSA; variably express calponin, podoplanin (recognized by D2-40), factor XIIIa, nuclear β-catenin, and cyclin D1; and focally express desmin {2712187; 2712186; 8804479; 1594491; 25025452; 23606697; 12873184; 9648161}. The Ki-67 proliferation index is < 5% {12873184}. The tumour is negative for cytokeratins, S100, follicular dendritic cell markers (CD21, CD23, CD35), vascular markers (CD31, CD34, von Willebrand factor [factor VIII–related antigen]), and KSHV/HHV8 {25025452; 17284119; 2712187; 27500890; 20181136; 21718465}.
FNA reveals bland, tapered, spindled cells with nuclear grooves surrounding an acellular matrix, and haemosiderin deposits {27027816; 26799943; 12462097}.

Essential: an intranodal benign spindle cell proliferation expressing actin(s); variably shaped dense collagenous bodies.

Desirable: nuclear β-catenin and/or cyclin D1 expression.
Intranodal palisaded myofibroblastoma is a benign neoplasm with a postsurgical local recurrence rate of about 6% {17284119}.
